title: Wootz crucible steel, southern India
summary: A source from the National Institute of Advanced Studies and the Indian Institute of Science dates the invention of crucible steelmaking in southern India to as early as 300 BCE. The megalithic site of Kodumanal in Tamil Nadu, about 300 BCE, may have been a crucible-processing site, with furnaces and a vitrified crucible fragment, though the evidence is preliminary.

uncertainty.note: Sources say "as early as 300 BC" and "c. third century BC". The evidence at Kodumanal is described as tentative or preliminary.

as_recorded.value: the invention of crucible steelmaking as early as 300 BC
Kodumanal, Tamil Nadu (c. third century BC)

where.historical_name: Kodumanal, near Karur in the Sangam-era Chera kingdom, southern India

importance.justification: Southern Indian crucible steel later supplied the high-carbon steel known as wootz.

reviewer_note: Least sure: the date and the site. Both sources share one author, and the Kodumanal link to crucible steel is called preliminary. The same sources describe wootz production as widespread across south India, so the single pin is only the earliest-evidence site.
